title: Establish atomic button surface contract and graceful degeneration
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Define and document an atomic "button surface" contract that unifies variant styling across themes, provides a clear token mapping for hover/press/loading/disabled states, and supplies fallback degeneration rules for older clients and edge cases (missing tokens, high-contrast mode, text-only platforms).

Scope:
- Author a single surface contract (surface-color, surface-border, surface-emphasis, surface-elevation) consumable by code and tokens.
- Replace ad-hoc overrides in Compact/Comfort variants with contract-driven styles.
- Specify degeneration rules: how a button should behave if a token is absent, when running on legacy browsers, or when animations are disabled.
- Provide explicit guidance for icon-only and mixed icon+label buttons (hit target, padding shrink, visual center).
- Add test matrix and QA checklist for regression scenarios observed in recent releases.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A design doc (Confluence) that describes the surface contract and token mapping for Primary, Secondary, Ghost, Link, and Destructive variants.
2) Figma token page updated with the new contract and examples (compact, comfort, icon-only).
3) Frontend component team obtains a single JSON token export that can be used to implement degenerations.
4) Regression checklist written and validated against at least three previously reported regressions (hover jitter, spinner overlap, focus outline misalignment).
5) UX review completed and sign-off from PM and Eng leads.

Trade-offs and notes:
- We deliberately avoid forcing a single color scheme; the contract is semantic and maps to theme palettes. Implementers can still opt into theme-specific overrides for brand needs.
- Degeneration rules favor accessibility (high-contrast, reduced-motion) over pixel-perfect parity.
- We will not touch token names used by older customers in this task; instead we provide a shim mapping guide for migration.

Links and artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/redwood/button-surface-contract-2026
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DS/Atomic+Button+Surface+Contract
- GitHub token export (pending): https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-tokens/pull/412
- Existing regression log: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/4865/Button+Regression+Incidents

Implementation notes for engineers (summary):
- Provide an exported JSON shape: {"surfaceColor":"string","surfaceBorder":"string","emphasis":"string","elevation":"string","spinnerZ":"number","pressOffset":"number"} (engineering to confirm exact shape).
- Ensure keyboard focus is tied to content box, not icon-only wrapper; update hit-area tests as described in QA checklist.
- Add unit tests for degeneration fallback order: explicit token -> theme palette -> neutral accessible fallback.
- Coordinate with runtime team for automated visual diffs on major theme toggles.
